findings.description: The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet rather than restricting it to known administrative IP ranges.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls such as a WAF or load balancer, unnecessarily exposing the instance directly to the internet.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no restriction on data exfiltration or command-and-control channels.

AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is readable by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions and is also committed to source control.
The instance does not configure metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of resources that may not need direct internet reachability.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of resources that may not need direct internet reachability.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true nor specify a KMS key, so data at rest on this volume is stored unencrypted by default.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving log data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, risking accidental public exposure or data loss of the netflow archive.
No versioning is configured on the bucket that stores flow logs, allowing log data to be overwritten or deleted without recovery, undermining the audit trail integrity.
